Currency Act
(Chapter 69)
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 29th December 2004 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

THE SCHEDULE
DESCRIPTION OF THE 2005 CHINESE ALMANAC COINS (YEAR OF THE ROOSTER) TO BE ISSUED ON 29TH DECEMBER 2004

Milled and Bearing the Words "MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE" and Lion symbol.
The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year date "2005" below it and the word "SINGAPORE" in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’clock for all the coins except for the $2 cupro-nickel and $1 gold coins.
Inspired by Chinese calligraphy, the rooster in the centre is symbolised by the appropriate Chinese character of the "Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches" to enhance the characteristics of the animal and the oriental cultural flavour. The peony, a traditional Chinese symbol of blessings and festive cheer, incorporated on the body of the rooster, ushers in the Lunar New Year. The 2 Chinese characters signifying the "Year of the Rooster" are on the right of the rooster design. The denomination of the coin in figures is below the design. The weight in troy Oz / grams and fineness of the coin are at the upper circumference for all the coins except for the $2 cupro- nickel coin.
